where: READING CHECK: "BISCUIT" AND "THE REEDS OF THE NORTH LAGOON" A q13
answer: The question asks how Kiran changes from the beginning of "Biscuit" to the end. At the beginning Kiran thinks cat-sitting will be easy and feels hurt when Biscuit hides from him; by the end he has learned to be patient and let Biscuit come to him in her own time. Early on, Biscuit hides even when he calls her and offers treats [4], and he takes it personally even though Mrs. Abara wrote, "Biscuit is shy with new people, so don't take it personally" [1]. At the end, "Biscuit was curled on the armchair, watching him" [7], and Kiran realizes she has been eating her food and getting used to him all along. The first evidence shows Kiran was trying too hard and doubting himself. The second shows that once he stopped pushing, Biscuit trusted him, so Kiran changed from impatient and unsure to patient and understanding.
note: Shy-pet arc plus quotes printed in q4 A [1] and q4 D [7].
